results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

The reverse outline, written without the spec, gives one summary per unit that matches the aligned spec paragraph's controlling idea in the spec's order for all 66 units (callout entries are apparatus and match no spec paragraph).
mobile.de: An Architecture Written in Its APIs ¶1: the outliner gave two ideas, but both are halves of p13's single controlling idea as the spec states it; the paragraph serves one idea.
mobile.de: An Architecture Written in Its APIs ¶12: the outliner gave two ideas, but both are halves of p24's single controlling idea as the spec states it; the paragraph serves one idea.
Autotrader UK: The Economics Disclosed ¶4: the outliner gave two ideas, but both are halves of p29's single controlling idea as the spec states it; the paragraph serves one idea.
CarGurus: Price Transparency as the Product ¶2: the outliner gave two ideas, but both are halves of p41's single controlling idea as the spec states it; the paragraph serves one idea.
Every unit ties to a supporting claim (A1 to A5) through its aligned spec paragraph or its section's advances_thesis; no unit is orphaned.

All tables (evidence, timeline, properties, ARPR, cross-case, trade-offs, verticals, evidence limits, patterns, Veldmark), Figures 1-6, the quoted manual and filing passages and the Golf scenario are introduced or followed by a sentence or caption saying what they show.

All transition_in boundaries were read in the draft; each expresses its declared relationship. The repaired boundaries (mobile.de, Autotrader, CarGurus and Failure Modes openings) now pick up the declared known information. The thinnest openings, carried by heading plus next topic, are Why Automotive Behaves Differently ¶1 (does not name the timeline or ladder), mobile.de ¶3, Autotrader ¶5 and ¶8 and Trade-offs ¶1; none lost either flow reader, so they are not failed.

The cold reader of the opening named the three questions, the evidence (integration manuals, investor reports, engineering posts for the four companies with OLX Autos as contrast), the tests of feed contracts, change feeds and model governance, and the close with Motorvane and Part IX's six cases, as expected.

The AC-1 reader gives every expected element: five-band ratings at mobile.de and CarGurus and Autotrader's price flags, mobile.de showing price against search position, the loop, owner, band-accuracy and boundary-clustering evaluation, no-rating path and ranking review; Deal Builder's 137,000 full reservations, H2 forecourt fall, cut stock, paused auto-rollout and 'request a reservation'; opt-in, per-dealer, reversible states; CarOffer and OLX Autos as retreats from owning cars.

The final section states what the six cases show together (supported, only not contradicted, silent), says why it matters (cite the record for layers, separability, contracts and governance; treat product convergence as an unproven bet), returns to the part introduction's test and hands off to the toolkit.
'The leaders are clear because they have to be' calls back to the hook, and ¶2 answers the part introduction's three-way test.
The introduction opens with a direct statement and the three properties; it is not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary opening, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', does not end on a rephrased thesis alone and holds no body evidence; its Part-level patterns are the spec's mandated Part IX close (the readers' difficulty with them is recorded under flow_is_followable).

results.quote: Autotrader's register of risks names "AI being used to disintermediate marketplaces"
results.finding: A quoted company fact appears for the first time here and names no source document or publication year (the risk register of the FY26 results, published 2026, is presumably meant); round 3's fix gave a year only for the audience figure that follows. Table rows elsewhere that restate facts sourced at first use were treated as cross-references and pass; no other unsourced company fact or unlabeled internal-system statement was found.

Organising principle: both readers describe the declared grouping (setup, companies, cross-case, application), the companies ordered by transaction-ladder reach with the two European listing platforms first, the cross-case comparison and the problem-solution close; neither marks any section's position unclear (reader A calls AutoScout24 'defensible by its stated reason'). Lost-thread points are recorded as separate results.

results.quote: mobile.de, CarGurus and Autotrader all publish five-band price ratings or price flags.
results.finding: Both readers read this as claiming five bands for Autotrader, which the body never supports (the cross-case table gives Autotrader only 'price flags'). Reader A item 2: 'on first reading it implies five bands for all three.'

results.quote: What it does show, in my reading, is an acquirer's platform absorbing another marketplace at the account and identity layer
results.finding: The previous unit says 'The post does not state the corporate relationship between the two companies', then this sentence calls AutoScout24 an acquirer without flagging it; reader A item 4: 'reads as a contradiction, or as an unflagged assumption.'

results.quote: Employee engagement fell from 91% to 72%.
results.finding: The figure sits among dealer-side rollout costs with no stated link to Deal Builder; reader A item 5: 'I re-read it to see whether it was a cause or a consequence of the rollout.'

results.quote: Trade press reported in December 2025 that the option lets a buyer ask for a reservation without paying the £99 fee.
results.finding: 'The £99 fee' presumes a fee never mentioned; ¶8, where the reservation is introduced, does not say a full reservation costs the buyer £99. Reader A item 6: '"The fee" presumes the reader knows a full reservation costs £99.'

results.quote: The documented defenses (insertion request IDs, serialized writes, dealer-owned inventory keys) exist because dealer feeds retry, overlap and arrive incomplete.
results.finding: No company's truncation or incomplete feeds are documented, none of the named defenses addresses truncation, and Where the Public Evidence Stops lists 'What happens when a full XML upload omits a car?' as unanswered; reader A item 8: 'The claim that the defenses exist because feeds "arrive incomplete" is not shown.'

results.draft_locus: Failure Modes the Record Exposes ¶1 (lead sentence)
results.quote: Where those options fail, as the last column of the table shows, the record exposes six risks:
results.finding: The pointer promises a one-to-one match with the trade-offs table's 'When it fails' column, but risks 4 (rollout) and 6 (new intermediaries) have no row there; reader A item 10: 'the sentence promises more than the table delivers.'

results.draft_locus: Comparing the Case to the Book's Patterns and to Veldmark ¶3
results.quote: Priya Raman's registry (the group model registry of Veldmark's head of data and ML), in the scenario's 9 November 2027 decision, is the place to record that the market-value model has two consumers, and Felix Brandt, Motorvane's CTO, the person to own its band-boundary monitoring.
results.finding: Two people, a registry and a dated decision arrive in one sentence whose second clause drops its verb; both readers had to re-read it. Reader A item 16: 'hard to follow on first reading.'

results.finding: The parenthesis splits subject from figure and the basis of €927 is never given (no subscription total is shown); reader A item 15: 'The reader has to work out that the €927 is not the obvious division ... I re-read it.'

results.quote: The public record supports sharing the uniform layers, contracts at the supply boundary, the search index as a rebuildable read model, models governed by the decision they drive, and separability under a change of owner.

The spec mandates the six-case synthesis; the draft can state the three-way test and tie each pattern to where this chapter touched it (AutoScout24's account consolidation, Motorvane's separate search), as reader B proposes.
